1. Primary Request and Intent:

The tool's landing page and results page look "AI-generated" due to default font/CSS choices. Daniel's requests evolved through the conversation:

   - Compare it against another AI-generated page (B-Roll guide) to identify shared AI tells
   - Create a specific design feedback document for just the resume tool
   - Build an interactive HTML comparison document where Daniel can visually compare current vs alternative design choices for every element
   - Include the results page elements too (score circle, severity badges, progress bars, issue cards, bank fit indicators, etc.)
   - Expand to 6 options per section, then 8 total per section
   - Use actual descriptive names instead of "Alt A, Alt B" etc.
   - Ensure correct font sizes and proper rendering
   - Add table of contents and mobile hamburger menu
   - Review work by taking screenshots to verify correctness
   - "keep iterating and checking work and making sure its both comprehensive and perfect"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - AI design pattern detection: DM Sans + Instrument Serif + DM Mono is the default AI font stack for "dark premium" sites
   - CSS anti-patterns that signal AI generation: 8-10px border-radius, navy-tinted dark backgrounds (#0A0C12), blue-gray text (#b8bfce), gradient progress bars, colored pill badges
   - Alternative design approaches: warm stone grays (#B5B0A8), true black backgrounds (#050505), sharp corners (2-3px radius), desaturated severity colors, monospace labels

     - All 14 Google Fonts loaded, all visuals rendered with inline styles

     - Written design feedback document with 8 numbered fixes specific to the resume tool

   - `/sessions/stoic-relaxed-carson/add_options.py`

     - Successfully added cards to all 20 sections
